title: Artuqids
capsule: The Artuqids were a Turkoman dynasty of the Oghuz Döger tribe founded by Artuk Bey, who governed Jerusalem for the Great Seljuks until his death in 1091; his sons established independent principalities in Upper Mesopotamia from 1101–1102, splitting into three branches at Hasankeyf (1102–1232), Mardin (1101–1409), and Harput (1185–1233). Ilghazi of Mardin inflicted the decisive Crusader defeat at Ager Sanguinis (28 June 1119), killing Prince Roger of Salerno, while Sökmen of Hasankeyf had earlier won at Harran (1104). The dynasty is also celebrated for commissioning Ibn al-Razzaz al-Jazari's Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices (1206), one of the most important medieval treatises on engineering. The last Mardin branch was extinguished by the Qara Qoyunlu in 1409.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territories of the three Artuqid branches are well documented in Arabic chronicles and modern scholarship; outer boundaries and zones of overlapping suzerainty with Seljuks, Zengids, and Ayyubids are less precisely mapped.
